cards.title: Project-local Developer Memory
cards.summary: Prototype a portable .dashgpt memory layer that can be understood by different coding agents.
cards.problem: Useful engineering context is fragmented across Copilot, OpenCode, Cline, local models and chat sessions.
cards.decision: Use a provider-neutral .dashgpt contract where cards are canonical memory and sessions are optional evidence.
cards.outcome: A repository can carry AI-readable engineering memory independently of which coding agent created it.

cards.title: Project State visualization
cards.summary: Make current DashGPT work understandable before drilling into individual memory cards.
cards.problem: The first prototype showed a semantic card gallery but did not clearly show what DashGPT itself is building now.
cards.decision: Make Project State the primary view: product spine, Now, Shipped/Active/Next and human workstreams.
cards.outcome: Opening developer mode should explain the current project in seconds; card details become the second level.

evidence.label: Project state was not legible from the initial card map

cards.title: Unified Card Dashboard — My Dash
cards.summary: Make canonical cards the primary personal surface and saved Dashes reusable semantic views.
cards.problem: Separate result-like surfaces make the product model harder to understand.
cards.decision: Keep cards canonical, make My Dash the virtual home view, and save semantic selections as Dashes.
cards.outcome: A user should see one coherent card surface instead of separate Results / Living Topics concepts.

cards.title: Coding-agent capture adapter
cards.summary: Let Copilot, OpenCode, Cline and other coding agents read/write the same project-local DashGPT memory.
cards.problem: The prototype still uses synthetic session data instead of receiving outcomes automatically from a coding agent.
cards.decision: Keep the core provider-neutral; add filesystem/CLI/MCP adapters as separate future capabilities.
cards.outcome: Planned: Agent A can finish work, .dashgpt retains the result, and Agent B can continue without the old full transcript.

cards.title: Share import regression safety net
cards.summary: Turn upstream ChatGPT Share format drift into automated CI signals.
cards.problem: Public share import could regress when upstream page formats or resolver behavior changed.
cards.decision: Keep deterministic parser coverage, browser flows and recurring production smoke fixtures together.
cards.outcome: Share-import regressions now fail automated checks instead of first appearing as user reports.

cards.title: Fresh Share backend resolver
cards.summary: Read current public Share JSON while preserving the normalized DashGPT chat contract.
cards.problem: A fresh public share was readable but DashGPT still classified it as unreadable.
cards.decision: Resolve current public share JSON and follow current-node ancestry before legacy fallbacks.
cards.outcome: Fresh Share links use the normalized conversation contract without mixing regenerated sibling branches.

cards.title: Chat-first onboarding
cards.summary: Create the first private card from the current AI conversation before exposing storage infrastructure.
cards.problem: Public share scraping was too fragile to be the first-value path for a new user.
cards.decision: Start from the current ChatGPT conversation and locally parse a portable distilled card envelope.
cards.outcome: A clean user can create a first private card without depending on a public Share URL.

cards.title: Structured Chat Continuation
cards.summary: Continue work in another AI with goal, decisions, constraints, current state and open questions.
cards.problem: A new AI chat could not continue useful work from a card title alone.
cards.decision: Transfer a Structured Continuation Brief with goal, facts, decisions, constraints, current state and open questions.
cards.outcome: Saved work can be resumed across AI clients without reconstructing the original conversation.

cards.title: Semantic Gallery UX
cards.summary: Keep related cards visually coherent while density changes without changing the selected memory.
cards.problem: Static storage-order cards did not feel like a memorable map of work.
cards.decision: Group by stable semantic signature and change density independently of selection.
cards.outcome: Related work forms stable visual neighborhoods that remain understandable on mobile and desktop.

cards.title: Semantic Dashes
cards.summary: Save useful semantic views over canonical cards without duplicating card content.
cards.problem: Cards from different chats needed to connect by meaning rather than conversation boundaries.
cards.decision: A Dash is a saved semantic view/group of canonical cards.
cards.outcome: Search-generated semantic views can be saved and reopened without creating parallel result objects.
